clue.text: Sailor's getting puncture that's plain

parts.note: an old salt is a seasoned sailor
a flat is a punctured tyre

explanation.surface: A sailor gets a flat tyre, which is plain to see.
explanation.definitionFit: A salt flat is a level expanse of salt-encrusted ground, a kind of plain.

clue.text: Poverty? Blow's reduced when given gold

indicators.note: cut short, so the final letter of the word for a blow is dropped

parts.note: a squall is a sudden gust, a blow of wind
or is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: Musing on whether poverty eases once a blow is softened by a gift of gold.
explanation.definitionFit: Squalor is the filth and wretchedness that go with extreme poverty, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Top swimming-pool left unfinished

indicators.note: a word left unfinished loses its last letter

parts.note: a lido is a public open-air swimming pool

explanation.surface: The top of a swimming pool has been left half built.
explanation.definitionFit: A lid is the top or cover of a container.

clue.text: Soldiers —- artillery favoured to capture leader of Turks without a doubt

parts.note: a force is a body of soldiers

indicators.note: the pair of pieces before it close around the next letter

parts.note: RA is the Royal Artillery

indicators.note: the first letter of the following word

parts.note: in favour, popular: in

explanation.surface: A military report: troops and favoured guns set out to seize the Turkish commander.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soldiers' is FORCE, not the usual OR or MEN; then RA and IN together capture T, giving RTAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: For certain is an idiom meaning definitely, beyond any doubt.

clue.text: Garden pest concealed beneath a pansy's head

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece placed beneath another comes after it
the head of a word is its first letter

parts.note: concealed means hid

explanation.surface: A garden pest lurks hidden under the bloom of a pansy.
explanation.definitionFit: An aphid, such as greenfly, is a sap-sucking insect gardeners treat as a pest.

clue.text: Riot squad's first and best

indicators.note: the first letter of the word before it

parts.note: the cream is the best part, the elite

explanation.surface: A riot squad's leading and finest officers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Riot' looks like part of 'Riot squad', but it is the definition: a riot or a scream is something hilarious.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally, both a riot and a scream mean a hilariously funny person or thing.

clue.text: Aquatic creature long dwelling in river

indicators.note: living inside, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: the Cam flows through Cambridge

explanation.surface: A water creature that has lived a long time in a river.
explanation.definitionFit: A clam is a bivalve mollusc living in water.

clue.text: Where tests are made to ensure sound quality

definitions.text: Where tests are made to ensure sound quality

parts.words: Where tests are made to ensure sound quality
parts.note: reads like a lab for checking that goods are sound, but sound here means acoustics: a room for testing reverberation

explanation.definitionFit: An echo chamber is a reverberant room used for acoustic testing and recording effects.

clue.text: Small change in Roman poet's description of wedding?

indicators.note: a slight rearrangement, two letters swapped, of the poet's name

parts.note: Martial was a Roman poet famous for epigrams

explanation.surface: A slight alteration in a Roman poet's account of a wedding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Small change' swaps the T and I of MARTIAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Marital is the adjective describing marriage, so it can describe a wedding, hence the question mark.

clue.text: New boy in Loot's final performance

indicators.note: the new-boy pair goes inside the word for loot

parts.note: swag is stolen goods, loot; Loot is also a play by Joe Orton
a son is a boy

explanation.surface: A new young actor appears in the farewell performance of Orton's play Loot.
explanation.definitionFit: A swan song is a last performance or work before retirement.

clue.text: Separate articles in range of lingerie not so good

indicators.note: each article goes inside the word for lingerie
the articles are inserted apart, at two different places

parts.note: underwear is the range of garments called lingerie
the is the definite article
a second copy of the definite article

explanation.surface: A range of lingerie of inferior quality sold as separate items.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Separate' signals that the two copies of the article go in at different places, not side by side; 'not so good' reads as a verdict on the lingerie but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Under the weather is an idiom meaning slightly unwell, not feeling so good.

clue.text: Word of mouth offering way to assist the disabled?

definitions.text: Word of mouth offering way to assist the disabled?

parts.words: Word of mouth offering way to assist the disabled?
parts.note: word of mouth is taken literally: words read from the movements of a speaker's mouth, helping deaf people

explanation.definitionFit: Lip-reading is understanding speech by watching the lips, a skill used by deaf people.

clue.text: Sort of cash bribe raised — lot asked, but a pound short

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised means the word is turned upwards, read backwards

parts.note: a sop is something given to pacify, a bribe

indicators.note: lacking, so the letter for a pound is removed

parts.note: a tall order is a lot to ask
L stands for a pound, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: A cash bribe is upped: a lot is being asked, though it's a pound short.
explanation.definitionFit: A postal order is a document bought at a post office for sending money, a form of cash.

clue.text: Glaswegian, say, heading away from race-track

indicators.note: the head, the first letter, goes away from the word

parts.note: Ascot is a famous English racecourse

explanation.surface: A man from Glasgow heads off from the races.
explanation.definitionFit: A Glaswegian is an example of a Scot, as signalled by 'say'.

clue.text: Homiletics developed from early history

indicators.note: the letters are worked into a new form

explanation.surface: The art of preaching evolved from ancient times.
explanation.definitionFit: Mesolithic describes the Middle Stone Age, a period of early prehistory.

clue.text: Came up to get central component of lottery award

parts.note: rose means came up

indicators.note: the central letters of the next word

explanation.surface: A winner comes forward to collect a lottery prize.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle three letters of LOTTERY give TTE.
explanation.definitionFit: A rosette is a ribbon badge awarded as a prize at shows.

clue.text: Vision certainly received by a number of boatmen

indicators.note: taken in by, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: an eight is a rowing crew of eight oarsmen
yes means certainly

explanation.surface: A rowing crew certainly had a vision.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyesight is the faculty of vision.

clue.text: In poll, are voters backing general?

indicators.note: the run is read backwards
the letters lie within the words that follow

explanation.surface: A pollster asks whether voters are supporting the general.
explanation.walkthrough: 'General' seems a military man; it is the adjective meaning all-round.
explanation.definitionFit: Overall and general both mean taking everything into account.

clue.text: Easily-damaged newspaper. kept in binder

indicators.note: one piece is held inside the other

parts.note: a file is a folder or binder
rag is a disparaging name for a newspaper

explanation.surface: A delicate old newspaper kept safe in a binder.
explanation.definitionFit: Fragile means easily broken or damaged.

clue.text: Hides, concealing admission of debt — how creditor feels?

indicators.note: the first piece hides the second within it

parts.note: furs are animal hides
an IOU is a note admitting a debt

explanation.surface: Someone hides an IOU, which enrages the lender.
explanation.definitionFit: Furious means very angry, as a lender might be when a debt is hidden away.

clue.text: Cheers fine cricket score

parts.note: good means fine
a bye is a run scored in cricket without the batsman hitting the ball

explanation.surface: Applause for a fine score in a cricket match.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheers is informal British for goodbye as well as thanks.

clue.text: Article is a regret after revolution in Turkey, and so on

indicators.note: the whole string is turned round, read backwards

parts.note: a is the indefinite article
rue means regret

explanation.surface: An article laments the aftermath of a revolution in Turkey.
explanation.definitionFit: Turkey and countries like it straddle Europe and Asia, the landmass called Eurasia.

clue.text: Source of river also running westward

indicators.note: in an across clue, going west means reading right to left

parts.note: too means also

explanation.surface: The source of a river that also flows west.
explanation.definitionFit: A root is the origin or source of something.

clue.text: It's useful to reflect on what may be coming up

definitions.text: It's useful to reflect on what may be coming up

parts.words: It's useful to reflect on what may be coming up
parts.note: sounds like advice to ponder the future, but means a device that literally reflects traffic approaching from behind

explanation.definitionFit: A wing mirror is a car's side mirror, showing vehicles coming up behind.

clue.text: Target of diet is right out of order

indicators.note: the letters are not in their proper order

explanation.surface: The aim of a diet is just wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: Girth is waist measurement, which a diet aims to reduce.

clue.text: Say "ah" when invited in by doctor

indicators.note: brought inside, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: a GP is a general practitioner, a family doctor
as means when

explanation.surface: A patient says ah when the doctor asks to look inside the mouth.
explanation.definitionFit: To gasp is to draw breath sharply, as when saying ah in surprise.

clue.text: Transport route connecting Hungerford and London?

definitions.text: Transport route connecting Hungerford and London?

parts.words: Transport route connecting Hungerford and London?
parts.note: a waterway personified: the river passes Hungerford Bridge in London and its catchment reaches near Hungerford in Berkshire

explanation.definitionFit: Old Father Thames is the personification of the River Thames, a historic route for river transport.

clue.text: Brit abroad upset cleaner

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, read backwards

parts.note: pom is Australian slang for a British person

explanation.surface: A British expat throws over the cleaner.
explanation.definitionFit: A mop is a cleaning tool.

clue.text: Form of text almost ready for acceptance by second court

indicators.note: taken in by, so the trimmed word goes inside
the last letter is dropped

parts.note: ripe means ready

explanation.surface: A text nearly ready for submission to a second court.
explanation.definitionFit: Script is handwriting or a form of written text.

clue.text: Young poultry's best served trimmed with a vegetable

parts.note: a chick is a young bird of the poultry yard

indicators.note: the last letter is cut off

parts.note: a peak is the highest, best point

explanation.surface: A chicken dish served with vegetables at its best.
explanation.definitionFit: A chickpea is a legume eaten as a vegetable.
